F1: group.add` calls `users.push` with no membership check, and the unique `(group_id, user_id)` index raises `RecordNotUnique`, which nothing rescues, so re-adding a member returns a 500 after earlier names were already added.
F2: group.users.delete(user_id)` deletes the join row without `Group#remove`, so neither the `user_count` counter cache nor the `primary_group_id` cleanup in `destroy_deletions` runs.
F3: Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1` gives one page too many when the count is an exact multiple of the limit, so "next" moves the offset to `user_count` and shows an empty page.
F4: removing the only row on the last page re-fetches at the old offset, which is now equal to the new total, so an empty page is shown with no automatic step back.
F5: the public members route now calls `findMembers()` with the default limit of 50, and `members.hbs` has no pager or load-more, so larger groups are cut off.
F6: limit` and `offset` go into the query after only `.to_i`, so negative values make PostgreSQL error (a 500), and `limit` has no cap.
F7: addMembers`/`removeMember` have no rejection handler in the controller or the model, so a 422, 404 or 500 gives the admin no feedback.
F8: the finding itself says the old `create` already ignored `alias_level`, so the change did not introduce this.
